anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers f1 because it explicitly unions the nine unique numbers, dedupes 101, drops 200/201/202 for draft/APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED, sorts by additions+deletions with the 88/130 tie broken by number, and closes with the exact `multi-PR mode takes at most 4 PRs (pi-cohort parallel.maxTasks); got 6` line followed by `discovered, smallest first: 101, 97, 112, 88, 130, 104`, while still stating no tracker init, continuation record, fetch, provisioning or dispatch ran. One thing to watch: After's output block repeats the cap message twice (once with the `gauntlet: stuck` marker prefix, once bare); since the fact only requires the bare line followed by the discovered line, this still holds, but the wording should make clear whether the marker line and the bare error line are both intended so future outputs don't collapse them into one and lose the exact bare line.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves f1 from fails to holds and regresses nothing: it keeps the draft/decided filters, the 101 dedup, the no-provisioning/no-dispatch/no-continuation/no-tracker-init statements, and adds the missing size-then-number sort and the exact two-line ending (`multi-PR mode takes at most 4 PRs (pi-cohort parallel.maxTasks); got 6` followed by `discovered, smallest first: 101, 97, 112, 88, 130, 104`), which Before lacked entirely (Before ended only with the cap line and never ordered the set). Two small hardening suggestions for the wording: name the review decisions explicitly (`APPROVED` for 201, `CHANGES_REQUESTED` for 202) rather than the collective "decided PRs", so a reader can check the filter rule directly, and phrase the "re-enter pi set routing" sentence as a hypothetical admission check (e.g. "the six discovered PRs would enter set routing, but the set exceeds parallel.maxTasks 4, so admission is rejected before any fetch, provisioning, or helper dispatch") to avoid any reading that routing actually began before the rejection.
